text: What was done and when, latest first.

$3$-torsion: $D_5=\gamma_5$ for every finite $3$-group with $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ of exponent $3$, whatever the invariants of $Q/\gamma_2$ (Theorem 6.9; Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 are its corollaries). Proved on paper and checked by an independent review; formally verified in Lean the same day, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1 (Lean). A minimal counterexample now has $\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)\ge9$ (instead of “two invariants $\ge9$”) and $\gamma_4\le Z$ cyclic.

A new version of the record PALOMAR-2026-10-23-000007 is registered in the Palomar registry (version 2, commit 508a336 of group-dimension): ten theorems now, with Theorem 6.9 added; Prop. 2.1 and Lemma 5.2(a)–(c) without additional hypotheses, the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7 with an explicit hypothesis (Prop. 5.3). The mechanical check passed and the automated (AI) review found no blocking problem.

$3$-torsion, continued: $D_5=\gamma_5$ whenever $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $3$-group, $\gamma_4^3\subseteq\gamma_5$ and $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$ (Theorem 6.10); $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_3/\gamma_4$ may have exponent $9$, and Theorem 6.9 is the special case. Proved on paper and checked by an independent review. Consequence: a minimal counterexample with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ has $x,y$ with $[x^9,y]\notin\gamma_4$. Of the $100$ groups with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ found earlier, the theorem covers $71$; in the first run of a targeted search ($68$ groups with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$, $21$ of them with $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$ and $47$ without) no candidate $z$ lies in $D_5$.

Gupta–Tahara at $p=3$ proved and formally verified: $D_5=\gamma_5$ whenever $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $p$-group, $p$ odd, and $[\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\subseteq\gamma_5$ (Theorem D.1), through Tahara's Theorem 6.1; metabelianity makes $\gamma_2$ a module over the commutative ring $\mathbb Z[G/\gamma_2]$, and the restriction $\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)=3$ is not needed. Checked by an independent review and in Lean, GuptaTaharaThree.lean; Lemmas 6.1 (at $p=3$) and 6.2 no longer rest on the hypothesis.

Theorem 6.10 ($\gamma_4^3\subseteq\gamma_5$, $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$) is formally verified: TaharaTheorem.lean, proof in ExpNine.lean; Theorem 6.9 is now derived from it. Its computations were redone: in the $1189$ groups of the targeted search with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ ($327$ with $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$, $862$ without) no candidate $z$ lies in $D_5$; the solver of Tahara's conditions gives $g=1$ in all of them and is non-vacuous in $847$; its negative controls (on $20$ earlier groups) also detect dropping (B) alone or (F) alone.

Version 3 of the record PALOMAR-2026-10-23-000007 is registered in the Palomar registry (commit add1be7 of group-dimension): thirteen theorems now, with Theorems 6.10 and D.1 added and, as a separate statement, Gupta–Tahara at $p=3$ (finite metabelian $3$-groups). The mechanical check passed and the automated (AI) review found no blocking problem.

A $2$-group with $D_4\ne\gamma_4$ has order $\ge2^{11}$ (the smallest known example is Rips's group, $2^{38}$). Order $2^9$ by a sieve over SmallGroups ($4\,421$ candidates), order $2^{10}$ by all $10\,208\,630$ parents of order $2^9$, with $n\in D_4$ a linear condition on the $p$-covering group. Code.

The Bartholdi–Mikhailov $3$-group with $D_7\ne\gamma_7$: order $3^{494}$ brought down to $3^{493}$ (three quotients by central subgroups of order $3$ not containing $\omega$); these three groups have cyclic centre, so none of their proper quotients keeps the witness. Subgroups: BM's argument applies to no section $H/N$ in which $\omega$ survives, for $\Phi(Q)\langle x_1,\dots,x_4\rangle\le HCode.

A $3$-group with $3$-torsion in some $D_n/\gamma_n$ has order $\ge3^9$: a reduction to a least-order example (cyclic centre, socle in $D_{c+1}\cap Q''\cap M_{c+1}$) and a run over all $3$-groups of order $3^6$–$3^8$ and class $\ge5$; class $4$ is the $D_5$ theorem up to $3^9$. Code.

The same bound raised to $3^{10}$: order $3^9$, class $\ge5$. A least-order example is a step-$1$ descendant of a group of order $3^8$; of $66\,569$ parents $4627$ pass the $p$-cover test, and all $27\,547$ descendants that pass the sieve have $D_{c+1}=1$; the descendant step was repeated with the fixed ANUPQ, with the same result. Code.

Lean: Lemma 6.2 — the minimal counterexample for $p=3$: a $3$-group of least order with $D_5\ne\gamma_5$ has class $4$, $Q''\ne1$, $d(Q)\ge3$, cyclic centre, $D_5(Q)=\Omega_1(Z(Q))=\langle z\rangle$ of order $3$ with $z\in Q''\cap M_5(Q)$, where $M_5=Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_3}(Q)^5)$, and $P_c(Q)=\langle z\rangle$, i.e. $Q$ is an immediate descendant of step size $1$ of $Q/\langle z\rangle$. Explicit hypotheses: Passi's $D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4$ and Gupta–Tahara's theorem ($D_{p+2}=\gamma_{p+2}$ for metabelian $p$-groups, $p$ odd). Lean.

Lean: Theorem 6.14, “⇒”: if a group $P$ of type $(d,2,1)$ with $P/\gamma_2$ elementary abelian ($p$ odd) is nonterminal in the sense of Lemma C.1 (some $Q$ has a central subgroup $\langle z\rangle$ of order $p$ with $Q/\langle z\rangle\cong P$ and $\gamma_4(Q)\ne1$), then (N1)–(N3) hold and (E)+(J) has a solution with $c=1$, for every choice of $u,v,w,x_i$ and of the exponents. No extra hypotheses; Lemma C.1 is still on paper only. Lean.

Lean: Theorem 6.14, “⇐”: if $P$ ($p$ odd, $\gamma_4=1$, $|\gamma_3|=p$) is generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$ with $|P/\gamma_2|=p^d$, a normal form $u,v,w,x_i$ is given, (N2) holds and (E)+(J) has a solution with $c=1$, then $P$ is nonterminal in the sense of Lemma C.1. With “⇒” this is the criterion relative to a given normal form. The group $Q$ is built not by a pc-presentation but by adjoining the $x_i$ one at a time to $\langle u,v,w,z\rangle$ as semidirect products with $\mathbb Z$; the Jacobi identity this needs has $z$-component (J), and its remaining part holds in $P$. Lemma C.1 is still on paper only. Lean.

Lean: the Lie algebra of Appendix A (Remark 6.4(2)): over any commutative ring the brackets $[e,k_i]=u_i$, $[k_1,k_2]=\rho$, $[k_1,u_2]=t$, $[k_2,u_1]=-t$, $[e,\rho]=2t$, $[e,t]=w$, $[u_1,u_2]=w$ define a Lie algebra generated by $e,k_1,k_2$; over any field it has type $(3,3,1,1)$ and $[\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\ne0$. So in the Lie analogue of Lemma 6.3 the hypothesis on $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ (at most two generators) is sharp: three do not suffice. Lean.

Lean: Gruenberg's theorem in the form Proposition 2.1 needs: in a finitely generated nilpotent group, an element none of whose odd powers is $1$ survives in some finite $2$-group quotient. Along the way, finitely generated nilpotent groups are residually finite (by induction on the class). Proposition 2.1 in Lean now has one hypothesis, Passi's theorem $D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4$. Lean.

Lean: Passi's theorem $D_4(G)^2\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group. The proof goes through Tahara's map $\psi_3$, already formalized for his Theorem 6.1: for $g\in D_4$ of a finite $p$-group of class $\le3$, Tahara's conditions give $g=\prod_{i\lt j}[x_i^{d(i)},x_j]^{u_{ij}d(j)/d(i)}$, and hence $g^2=1$; the general case goes through Sylow subgroups, finite generation and residual finiteness. Proposition 2.1 and Remark 2.3 are now proved in Lean without hypotheses, and Lemma 6.2 keeps one, Gupta–Tahara's theorem. Lean.

Rips's group from Tahara's 1978 presentation: $D_4=\{1,y_1^{128}\}$; every proper subgroup and every quotient checked has $D_4=1$, so the sections checked give no calibration below $2^{38}$ (proper sections $H/N$ not checked). Code.

The statement on candidates in Prop. 5.7 now has an elementary proof: every candidate has $|\Phi(Q)|\ge16$, i.e. rank $\le\log_2|Q|-4$. The classification of the groups of order $2^9$ and rank $8$ and the computation of their descendants are no longer needed (they remain as checks). Lean proves that no candidate has $|P_2(Q)|\le8$, and also proves Lemma 5.6. Consequence: a counterexample of order $2^{12}$, if any, has rank $\le8$.

Lean: Jennings' theorem in the case needed — $D_5(Q)\le Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}(Q)^5)\le Q^8\gamma_2^4\gamma_3^2$ for finite $2$-groups of class $\le3$ (via the Jennings basis and the Lazard series); Lemma 5.2(a)–(c) given $D_3=\gamma_3$; the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7 given $D_3=\gamma_3$ and Prop. 5.3.

The Lean formalization has been ported to Lean/Mathlib v4.35.0 with the module system and submitted to the Palomar registry: nine theorems (Theorems 6.6 and 6.8, Lemma 5.6, the two statements of Prop. 5.7 on candidates, Jennings' inclusion, and three conditional ones: Prop. 2.1, Lemma 5.2(a)–(c), the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7); the mechanical check passed and the automated (AI) review found no blocking problem; registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-23-000007.

Certificates for Prop. 5.3: each of the $3400$ groups of order $2^{10}$, given by its pc presentation, comes with a finite module and matrices; Lean checks the relations, that all products of four $(g-1)$ vanish, and faithfulness, hence $D_4=D_5=1$ and order $2^{10}$. The $3400$ checks run as compiled code (native_decide), not in the kernel; the soundness of the checker (a passing check gives a faithful representation killing $\Delta^4$) is proved in Lean and kernel-checked. The completeness of the list is Lemma 5.2(d) and the ANUPQ computation. Data and scripts.

Lean: Theorem 6.12 ($P^{*\prime\prime}=1$; for every central extension by a subgroup of exponent $p$, since Mathlib has no $p$-covering group), Remark 2.2, Lemma 5.2(d) (a minimal counterexample is an immediate descendant of step size $1$) and Lemma 6.11 (the filter on parents). The remaining paper results and the classical hypotheses ($D_3=\gamma_3$, the theorems of Passi and Gruenberg) are next in the formalization plan.

Lean: $D_3(G)=\gamma_3(G)$ for every group (Higman, Rees, Passi). For finite groups from the formalized Theorem 4.1 of Tahara, in general via finite generation and finite quotients of finitely generated groups of class $\le2$. The hypothesis $D_3=\gamma_3$ is dropped from Proposition 2.1, Remark 2.3, Lemma 5.2, Proposition 5.7 and the derivation of Proposition 5.3 from the certificates.

Lean: Lemma 6.1 — $D_{p+2}(Q)\subseteq Q''\cap M_{p+2}(Q)$, where $M_n=Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_p}(Q)^n)$, for finite $p$-groups of class $\le p+1$, $p$ odd; for $p=3$ and $D_5\ne1$ this gives $Q''\ne1$ and $d(Q)\ge3$. Gupta–Tahara's theorem ($D_{p+2}=\gamma_{p+2}$ for metabelian $p$-groups, $p$ odd) is an explicit hypothesis; its wording was checked against the scan of the original. Lean.
The preprint is submitted to arXiv (math.GR).

An exact criterion for nonterminality of $p$-groups of type $(d,2,1)$ (Theorem 6.14): proved on paper for odd $p$ and elementary $P/\gamma_2$, checked by computer at $3^8$, $3^7$, $5^7$, $7^7$. The question is removed from the open ones.
In the paper: an explicit Lie algebra of type $(3,3,1,1)$ with $[M_2,M_2]\ne0$ over $\mathbb F_p$ for every odd $p$ (Appendix A); the full case $a=2$ of Theorem 6.8 (Appendix B).

A repeat with ANUPQ with the audit fixes: the $2^{10}$ search (all $858$ chunks, $3400$ candidates and the lattice answers) and ranks $2$–$4$, $7$, $8$ of order $2^{11}$ agree exactly with the old runs. The caveat on orders $2^{10}$ and $2^{11}$ is lifted.
$2^{11}$, rank $5$: $824$ candidates, all with $D_4=D_5=1$ (about $83$ CPU-hours, part of them on BOINC). Order $2^{11}$ is settled: a counterexample, if any, has order $\ge2^{12}$ (Prop. 5.10).

Lean: Tahara's Theorem 6.1 (the description of $D_5$ for finite groups of class $\le4$) is proved in Lean, with no sorry and only the standard axioms; Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 are now proved in Lean with no hypotheses. The formalization found a typo in our transcription of Tahara's condition (C₂); it was fixed before the proof.
$2^{11}$, rank $6$: $13$ candidates, all with $D_4=D_5=1$.
